# Code blocks and executable-example presentation {#sec-code-blocks}

This chapter defines how source code, terminal transcripts, patches, and
source/output examples appear without tying the manuscript to a PDF backend.
Every fixture uses ordinary fenced-code attributes and semantic containers.

## Syntax highlighting and filenames {#sec-code-filenames}

A filename identifies the source context without becoming part of the copied
code. Language tags drive syntax highlighting; color is supplementary because
keywords, punctuation, and the original text remain visible without it.

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`counter.py`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.python}
def clamp(value: int, lower: int, upper: int) -> int:
    """Return value constrained to the inclusive interval."""
    return max(lower, min(value, upper))
```
:::

## Opt-in line numbers {#sec-code-line-numbers}

Line numbers help prose discuss a fixed specimen but are omitted by default so
short examples remain easy to copy. The numbers are presentation, not literal
characters in the source.

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`counter.py`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.python code-line-numbers="true"}
def count_enabled(flags: list[bool]) -> int:
    total = 0
    for enabled in flags:
        if enabled:
            total += 1
    return total
```
:::

## Line callouts and annotations {#sec-code-annotations}

Inline callout markers connect explanations to source lines. HTML turns them
into interactive annotations, while the other outputs preserve a readable
labeled list.

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`status.py`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.python}
def status_code(load: int) -> int:
    bounded = max(0, min(load, 100))  # <1>
    if bounded >= 90:                 # <2>
        return 2
    if bounded >= 70:
        return 1
    return 0
```
1. Clamp untrusted input before applying the thresholds.
2. Test the most severe condition first.
:::

## Long-line policy {#sec-code-long-lines}

Interactive HTML preserves source columns with horizontal scrolling. EPUB and
fixed-page outputs wrap long lines because clipping or shrinking an entire
listing would make content inaccessible. A visual continuation is never a new
source line. Authors should still prefer readable source and use an intentional
long line only when the unbroken value matters.

The first fixture wraps at ordinary spaces. The second is an intentionally
unbroken token that requires an anywhere-safe fallback in the PDF and EPUB
paths.

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`spaced-line.txt`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.text}
ALKAHEST SPACED LINE BEGIN 0123456789 0123456789 0123456789 0123456789 0123456789 0123456789 SPACED LINE END
```
:::

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`unbroken-token.txt`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.text}
ALKAHEST_LONG_LINE_BEGIN_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_LONG_LINE_END
```
:::

## Patches and terminal sessions {#sec-code-diff-terminal}

A diff retains its conventional `+`, `-`, and context prefixes, so additions
and removals do not depend on color. A terminal transcript uses a visible
prompt and includes output in reading order. Commands intended for copying
should also appear separately when prompts would be inconvenient.

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`counter.patch`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.diff}
diff --git a/counter.py b/counter.py
--- a/counter.py
+++ b/counter.py
@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@
 def next_value(current: int) -> int:
-    return current + 1
+    maximum = 255
+    return min(current + 1, maximum)
```
:::

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`terminal`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.console}
$ python3 counter.py --start 41
42
$ printf 'done\n'
done
```
:::

## Executable-example presentation {#sec-executable-presentation}

An executable example is presented as a named source block followed immediately
by its expected standard output. Both remain static, reviewable manuscript
content: normal, CI, preview, and release builds do not execute code. Authors
use dotted language classes such as `{.python}`; executable cell syntax such as
`{python}` is rejected before rendering. This keeps cloning or publishing a
book from granting its manuscript ambient command execution. Declarative
`{mermaid}` and Graphviz `{dot}` diagram cells are the only machine-locked
exceptions and do not grant a general-purpose command interface.

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`checksum.py`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.python}
values = (3, 1, 4, 1, 5)
print(sum(values))
```
:::

::: {.code-with-filename}
[`standard output`]{.code-with-filename-file}

```{.text .code-output}
14
```
:::

The source/output pair is deliberately small enough to verify by inspection.
If a separate opt-in verifier is added later, it must run offline in a locked
environment with read-only sources, disposable outputs, explicit resource
limits, and output-drift checks. Publication caching and frozen execution
results remain disabled; generated results must stay distinguishable from
commands and authored prose.
